exposure: Sociodemographic factors (parity, race/ethnicity, education, marital status, income, receipt of public assistance, nativity)
Biomedical conditions (obesity, hypertensive disorders, diabetes mellitus)
Behavioral factors (multivitamin supplement intake, support from father of baby, support from family, major stress in pregnancy, cigarette smoking, alcohol intake)
cohort: 8509 women enrolled in the Boston Birth Cohort, a predominantly Black population
finding: Increasing maternal age was independently associated with higher odds of spontaneous preterm birth, cesarean delivery, and low birth weight, even after adjusting for sociodemographic, biomedical, and behavioral factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section deliveries were higher among women 30 years or older, even after adjusting for various factors.
